Subject: Dedicated GPU pool — initial sizing context

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for taking time last week. We scoped an internal spike and pulled some basic telemetry — attaching a small sample (helix-workload-sample.csv). A few high-level notes: average requests per minute currently ~240 RPM, peak short bursts to ~1,200 RPM (90th pct over 30s), typical context length 1,024 tokens, median generated tokens ~160, synchronous chat latency requirement ~250ms p50, tolerant to p95 up to 1s.

We're evaluating a 12–18 month reserved commit for predictability and are most interested in a pricing example and recommended GPU pool size for a production rollout (start with 10k daily active users, projected 3x growth in 12 months). Also need guidance on throughput guarantees and failure/fallback behavior.

Can you advise on what data you need and whether Redwood recommends a dedicated pool vs hybrid reserved + burst?

Thanks,
Asha Mehta
VP Engineering, Helix AI

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — initial sizing context

Hi Asha — great data, thanks. Quick answers and next steps below.

What we need to size accurately:
- steady-state RPS (requests/sec) and distribution across hours of day
- typical prompt+gen token counts (you gave context ~1,024 and gen ~160 — perfect)
- concurrency pattern (are requests evenly spread or user-driven bursts?)
- latency SLO target (you mentioned p50 250ms)

Initial recommendation (ballpark, based on sample):
- Start with a 4x A100-equivalent GPU pool (roughly 4 GPUs) configured for medium-latency chat workloads with continuous batching and KV cache enabled. That should handle ~300 RPS steady with headroom for bursts (observability will guide exact autoscale/burst settings).
- Reserved commit: 12-month term with 20% discount off list for upfront commit; higher discounts available for multi-year or larger commits.
- Throughput guarantee: we can commit to committed capacity availability SLA and offer burst credits for temporary overage. We'll scope exact numbers after we see 48–72h of representative traffic.

Ben (cc'd) will draft a more detailed sizing sheet (including token-month estimate) and an XLS with GPU pool scenarios. Can you share daily/hourly breakdown for the last 14 days if possible?

Happy to run a 2-week sizing pilot on Dedicated (metered, credit-based) so you can validate latency & cost.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Asha, Priyom — I ran the numbers from the CSV and a few sensible assumptions. Short summary below, full workbook attached.

Assumptions used:
- average requests: 240 RPM = 4 RPS steady; baseline concurrency ~6 concurrent requests per second after accounting for bursts and retries; peak burst modeled at 1,200 RPM = 20 RPS for ~30s windows.
- prompt length: 1,024 tokens + 160 generated = 1,184 tokens / request.
- model profile: half of traffic will hit a 20B variant, half a 7B faster quantized variant (mixed-model routing).

Monthly token estimate (approx):
- 4 RPS steady * 86,400s/day * 30d * 1,184 tokens ≈ 12.3B tokens/month baseline
- With 3x growth in 12 months -> ~37B tokens/month peak.

GPU sizing scenarios:
- Conservative start (validation): 4x A100-eq GPUs — good for development-to-production, ~300 RPS effective with mixed models, expected p50 latency ~180–300ms depending on batching.
- Production baseline (recommended for initial GA): 10x A100-eq GPUs — handles sustained 1k RPS with room for model variant routing and background caching. With autoscale + burst pool this maps to your peaks.
- Aggressive (cost-optimized at scale): 16x A100-eq with heavier quantization on 7B branch and larger KV cache — best for sustained high-throughput chat with many concurrent contexts.

Pricing / commit guidance:
- 12-month commit (10 GPU equivalent): baseline list $X/GPU/mo. We can offer: 18% discount for a single-year 10-GPU commit + 6% credit for a no-cost 2-week sizing pilot that converts.
- 24-month commit: 25% discount with a 5% additional technical support credit.

Operational notes:
- We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for prompts that have repetition; this drops token cost significantly.
- Smart routing: route low-latency queries to the quantized 7B variant and heavier generation to the 20B.

I'll upload the workbook with scenario tabs. If you want, we can run a short pilot with A/B routing to measure actual p95 and token consumption before final commit.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: gpu-sizing-estimate.xlsx (full workbook)

Asha — looping in pricing and finance (Lauren) to confirm discount structure and packaging. Clarifications we need from Helix to finalize a binding quote:
- Target committed GPU-equivalent count (do you want our Production baseline (10 GPU-eq) or start smaller)?
- Preferred term (12 vs 24 months).
- Are you planning to use Redwood Dedicated only (private VPC) or Dedicated + Hosted overflow? Overflow affects discount bands.

Preliminary offer we can move to SOW:
- 12-month commit, 10 GPU-eq pool + 4 GPU-eq burst credit bucket.
- Discount: 20% off list for 12-mo (10 GPU) if signed within 30 days.
- Additional 5% discount if Helix prepays 3 months up front.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for committed capacity; overage billed at a reduced burst rate and first 10% overage covered by burst credits.

Next steps: if Helix is comfortable with the 10-GPU baseline and 12-month term, we'll draft an SOW and send a DocuSign for signature. We'll include a 2-week sizing pilot clause that converts credits into the contract if you proceed.

-Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
